remediation.detailInspect: 1) Inspect which base image and fixed packages Docker Scout recommends:
remediation.detailMeaning: --only-fixed means a package fix exists; it does not guarantee that a ready replacement image tag exists.
remediation.detailFirstParty: 2) First-party image: update its base image and dependencies in source, rebuild it, push an immutable candidate, and scan that candidate.
remediation.detailThirdParty: Third-party image: select a maintained patched upstream tag, resolve its digest, and scan that exact candidate.
remediation.detailVex: If a finding is genuinely not exploitable, document a reviewed VEX exception instead of silently ignoring it.
remediation.detailSourceUnverified: The deployment path is identified, but its source is stale or could not be rendered with the active .env. Reconcile it manually; automatic source editing is disabled.
remediation.detailEditReview: Review the declarative change before deployment:
remediation.detailDeploy: 4) Deploy the owning stack after any required backup:
remediation.detailQuickStart: 4) Use the owning repository's quick-start menu to render, review, and deploy the stack:
remediation.detailUnknown: 3) Deployment source is unresolved ({reason}). Do not guess a file; rerun and review the mapper:

remediation.locationPrompt: Open the shown deployment directory in another terminal, then press Enter to continue (q cancels):
remediation.detailRuntimeWarning: A direct service update is temporary configuration drift. Prefer fixing declarative source; use this only as a guarded emergency action:
remediation.detailVerify: 5) Verify service tasks and rescan every image:
